errors.text: The proposed rise in HCP atom fraction is treated as evidence of amorphization, although HCP-classified atoms in an FCC alloy commonly indicate stacking faults or partial-dislocation activity rather than amorphous structure.
The hypothesis predicts stacking-fault annihilation while also predicting a significant increase in HCP atoms, creating an unresolved internal inconsistency.

Endpoint HCP counts and dislocation line lengths alone cannot distinguish thermal disorder from mechanically induced annealing because both mechanisms may reduce measured dislocation length; a thermal-only or no-indentation control is required.
